title: Magnetic Declination Calculator: Compass North
description: Find the magnetic declination for any place with the Magnetic Declination Calculator — WMM 2025 based, with true-to-magnetic bearing conversion. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, in New York the compass needle points about 12.7 degrees west of true north in 2025 — hike a 'north' bearing uncorrected there and you drift more than 200 metres off line per kilometre.
quick_answer: The Magnetic Declination Calculator gives the angle between true north and magnetic north for any location, calculated from the World Magnetic Model 2025. Search a place or click the map and read the declination — plus how to convert map bearings to compass bearings.

body.t: Every bearing taken from a map is true; every bearing walked is magnetic. The declination is the translation — skip it and a 5 km leg in New York ends some 1,100 m from its intended line. Pair with the
Courses are set in one north and walked in the other. This page supplies the local figure instructors write on the board — and explains why it expires.
Panels and dishes are aimed by compass more often than by survey. Correct the compass with the declination or the 'south-facing' array faces south-west by twelve degrees.
Old surveys were run on the magnetic north of their day — in parts of the US that differs from today's by several degrees. The model's current figure frames how far the old needle has wandered.

examples.label: Example · Converting a bearing in New York

body.t: Declination ≈ 12.7°W (2025). Map bearing 090° (due east, true). Magnetic bearing = true − declination = 090 − (−12.7) = 102.7° — set about 103° on the compass. Walk 090 on the dial instead and you walk a line rotated nearly 13° off the map's.

examples.label: Example · Los Angeles, the other sign

body.t: Declination ≈ 11.4°E. The same true 090° becomes magnetic 090 − 11.4 = 78.6°. East declination subtracts, west adds — 'East is least, west is best' as the mnemonic has it (for converting true to magnetic).

popular_table.title: Approximate declination, 2025 (WMM — values drift yearly)
popular_table.intro: Rounded from the World Magnetic Model — check your exact spot on the calculator, and expect roughly a tenth of a degree of yearly change in many regions.
popular_table.note: The agonic line (zero declination) currently runs through the US Midwest-to-Southeast and near the UK. London's needle pointed about 24° W in 1800, crossed true north in the mid-2010s, and now sits slightly east — declination is a moving target by design.

faq: Declination is the Earth's doing (true versus magnetic north). Deviation is your compass's local error from nearby metal, vehicles and electronics. This page prices the planet's part; the compass's part is cured by distance from iron, not by models.
Why does my hiking app show a different number?

Apps vary in model vintage (WMM updates every five years) and rounding. A few tenths of a degree between sources is normal; several degrees means one source is stale — WMM 2025 is the current edition.

On maps with a grid (UTM, National Grid), grid north differs slightly from true north away from the grid's central meridian — a small, printed-on-the-map correction (convergence) that careful navigators stack with declination.
Can I use a 10-year-old map's declination note?
The diagram is a museum piece: US declinations drift roughly 0.05–0.1° per year in many areas, so a decade-old figure can be a degree off — hundreds of metres on a long leg. Use the current model.
Is declination the same at altitude or underground?
The field direction varies smoothly; at aircraft altitudes the change is small for navigation purposes, but mines and surveys use local measurements where the work demands them.

Declination is defined worldwide by the same model — near the magnetic poles it swings wildly and compasses become useless for direction, which polar travellers plan around with grid and gyro methods.
Phones fuse magnetometer, gyro and GPS; their 'true north' toggle usually applies this same model internally. Knowing the local figure lets you audit the phone rather than trust it blind.
